Barton — thanks for the manifest. I put together a concise "validated deliverable" checklist below and attached the signed_bundle_manifest.yaml and our public-signing-key.pem. Summary:

High-level flow (brief):
1) Redwood signs the release bundle in an HSM-backed offline environment (YubiHSM2 + isolated signing host).
2) We produce both an artifact tarball and a small signed manifest YAML that contains SHA256 checksums for every image and a detached signature file.
3) Artifact is shipped via vetted courier. Field operator runs the verification script that checks checksums, verifies the detached signature against the public key, and performs minimal smoke tests (kernel boot, agent handshake).

Acceptance checklist (to present to SOC2 / EdgeCorp on arrival):
- manifest present and matches courier manifest (edgecorp_media_manifest.csv).
- sha256 checksums match for: signed-bundle.tar.gz and package images (list in signed_bundle_manifest.yaml).
- detached signature verifies: gpg --verify signed-bundle.sig signed-bundle.tar.gz (or openssl dgst -sha256 -verify public-signing-key.pem -signature signed-bundle.sig signed-bundle.tar.gz).
- signer identity: key fingerprint 3A:9F:5C:11:4E:2B:7D:9C:44:AA:EE:21:17:6C:A3:2B:45:9D:E8
- signing key stored in HSM; private key never leaves isolated host.
- boot smoke test: VM boots to runlevel 3, agent registers to the customer control plane over the private peering link (no inbound required).
- post-acceptance: operator sends signed acceptance email + scanned courier manifest to support@redwood.ai; Redwood will countersign using DocuSign (link below).

Operational notes / commands for field operator (include in README on USB):
- sha256sum signed-bundle.tar.gz
- openssl dgst -sha256 -verify public-signing-key.pem -signature signed-bundle.sig signed-bundle.tar.gz
- ./verify-offline.sh --manifest signed_bundle_manifest.yaml

Acceptance authority: Marissa Cole (Director, Deployment Ops) will be listed as Redwood acceptance authority. If she's not available on-site, Rishi Malhotra (SRE lead) is delegated.

Attachment: signed_bundle_manifest.yaml (1.6kB)
Attachment: public-signing-key.pem (2.4kB)
Related link: https://docusign.com/edgecorp/acceptance/xyz123

Let me know what else you need and I can add step-specific expected outputs (sample hash lines) to the manifest file.

— Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Program Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Adding a couple of technical clarifications for the verification script and smoke test so field ops and EdgeCorp SRE have deterministic expectations:

Verification script behavior (verify-offline.sh):
- exit codes: 0 = all checks passed; 1 = checksum mismatch; 2 = signature invalid; 3 = missing artifact
- outputs a small JSON file verification-report.json with keys: sha256_ok, sig_ok, boot_probe_ok (true/false) and operator_note (string). We will include a human-readable summary at the top of the script.

Signature format:
- We'll produce a detached signature using OpenSSL (RSA 3072) for the tarball and GPG v2 for image-level artifacts. Both options are supported for on-site verification; the manifest includes the expected method per-entry.

Boot smoke test:
- After tarball install, systemd target multi-user (network-online.target) must be reached within 120s.
- Agent will attempt an outbound TLS handshake to a pre-configured control-plane VIP. We will accept successful TLS handshake plus token exchange as agent ready.

Edge cases: if the site has an enforced egress proxy, the operator should toggle the agent into 'fallback-proxy' mode; the verify script will surface this as operator_note and still allow acceptance if signature and checksum validate.

I'll attach verify-offline.sh (stub) to help their SREs run a dry run.

Attachment: verify-offline.sh (430 bytes)

— Priyom
Senior Release Engineer, Redwood Inference
